chapters.title: StockReef, live on Robinhood Chain testnet
chapters.speaker: Aryan
phrases: This is StockReef, running live on Robinhood Chain.
It lets you borrow dollars against your Tesla stock tokens,
and it keeps that loan safe when the stock market closes for the weekend.

chapters.title: What goes wrong on weekends
chapters.speaker: Aryan
phrases: Tesla's token can be traded all weekend, but the real stock market closes on Friday afternoon.
If Tesla opens much lower on Monday, a loan can go bad before anyone can react.

chapters.title: Today, lenders ignore the weekend
chapters.speaker: Aryan
phrases: Three billion dollars of stocks are on chain, yet almost none are borrowed against.
Today's apps use one safety limit all week, even before a weekend.
In a big weekend drop, that costs lenders four times more.

chapters.title: The live app, with real loans
chapters.speaker: Awaan
phrases: I connect the borrower's wallet to the live app.
The portfolio shows the whole loan on one page, with every safety check.
On the lending page you can see four real loans and what each one is worth.
And the operations page shows who needs to act before Friday's close.

chapters.title: Two hours before the close
chapters.speaker: Awaan
phrases: Two hours before the market closes, StockReef starts lowering the safe limit,
from eighty percent down to seventy.
At quarter past three, this loan is just over the new limit.
So the app says exactly what to do: pay back about seven dollars by three thirty.

chapters.title: Paying back before the close
chapters.speaker: Awaan
phrases: This borrower set aside some money in advance, for exactly this moment.
I click run, and a real transaction goes to Robinhood Chain.
It confirms in seconds. The debt drops from seventy two to sixty five dollars.
The loan is safe again, and no stock was sold.
And here is the receipt, on the public Robinhood Chain explorer.

chapters.title: No money set aside? A partial trim
chapters.speaker: Awaan
phrases: Ben didn't set any money aside, and his loan is now over the limit.
So someone else pays off part of his loan, and gets a small two percent reward.
Ben's loan shrinks from thirty dollars to eighteen, and stays open.
A partial trim, not a full liquidation, and it's on chain too.

chapters.title: The weekend, then Monday
chapters.speaker: Aryan
phrases: At four o'clock the market closes, and new borrowing is switched off.
But paying back still works, so the borrower pays back one dollar on chain.
On Monday morning a new price arrives, but StockReef waits five minutes before trusting it.
Then it checks every loan again.
Cleo's loan is now over the limit, so part of it is paid off first.
Only then can people borrow again.

chapters.title: Lenders are protected
chapters.speaker: Aryan
phrases: Lenders are protected too.
Their share always shows what the loans are really worth.
If Tesla fell to two hundred twenty dollars, lenders would see the loss right away, shared fairly.
Nobody gets a surprise later.

chapters.title: Breaking it on purpose
chapters.speaker: Awaan
phrases: Now let's break something on purpose.
The price feed has stopped for two minutes.
I try to borrow one dollar.
The contract says no, because the price is out of date, and my wallet is never even asked to sign.

chapters.title: Code that holds up
chapters.speaker: Awaan
phrases: Behind the app, five hundred thirty one automated tests run in about a minute.
They try to break the risky parts, and they all pass.
Four more run against the real Tesla token.

chapters.title: Next for StockReef
chapters.speaker: Aryan
phrases: Next, we tune the limits using years of real weekend price data,
add more stocks one by one,
get a security audit, and launch on Robinhood Chain mainnet.
StockReef: borrow against your stocks, safely, even when the market is closed.
